answer: Each agent identity is one vertex in a work graph, and joining costs a refundable bond locked per vertex. A vertex only earns reputation when established peers attest its completed work, and it must keep sending a signed pulse of fresh verified work or its standing decays. Reputation flows like a tide: it rises only from real, attested transactions and drains away from idle or isolated vertices. An attacker forging a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand bonds and sustain a thousand streams of verifiable work, while the bond of any vertex caught cheating is slashed.
